title: What does a trillion dollars actually mean?

basedOn.title: Trillions – What is a trillion dollars?

methodology.copyrightNote: Original Power Atlas wording and interactive chart; linked graphics are inspirations and research leads, not reproduced images.
methodology.stockVsFlow: Never rank a stock, such as wealth or debt outstanding, against annual spending as though they are commensurate or additive.
methodology.scope: Geography matters: global values, U.S. values and developing-country values must stay labeled.
methodology.nominalDollars: Numbers are nominal USD reported by the named source in their cited year or fiscal year; no implied inflation adjustment.
methodology.projection: Projections and estimates must be labeled and not treated as realized spending.
methodology.causality: Neither concentration nor a large number alone establishes monopoly, collusion, policy capture, wrongdoing, inflation, or a household premium. Investigate mechanisms with independent market, policy and transaction evidence.
methodology.comparativeMethodologies: Do not combine IISS and SIPRI defense estimates; they use different inclusion and classification methods.
methodology.explainLocalConnection: No ZIP-level causal effect asserted; only source-backed macro context until joins are tested.
methodology.gdpSeparation: GDP is nominal annual value added; keep in its own annual-output view rather than treating as wealth, money stock, tax revenue or discretionary funds.

metrics.label: Combined billionaire wealth
metrics.definition: Forbes list total of 3,428 individuals; net-worth estimate based on March 1, 2026 values.
metrics.interpretation: Wealth stock is primarily asset valuations, not available cash; does not imply a specific price premium.

metrics.label: U.S. billionaire wealth
metrics.interpretation: Overlaps with the global billionaire total; do not add them.

metrics.label: Global debt outstanding
metrics.definition: IIF global debt stock as of end-2025 across sectors.
metrics.interpretation: Liability-stock across many sectors; debt can finance investment and is not equivalent to a single annual bill.

metrics.label: U.S. household debt outstanding
metrics.sourcePublisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
metrics.definition: New York Fed Consumer Credit Panel total debt balance; rounded figure.
metrics.interpretation: A debt stock, not annual household debt service; does not establish debt was caused by market concentration.

metrics.label: U.S. federal spending
metrics.interpretation: Annual spending, not a stock of cash; separate from corporate capitalization.

metrics.label: U.S. healthcare spending
metrics.definition: CMS/Health Affairs projection for calendar-year 2025, not final historical actual.
metrics.interpretation: Includes public and private expenditure; overlaps with federal spending; chart's $5.3T was 2024, not 2025.

metrics.label: Global defense spending — IISS
metrics.definition: IISS estimate of global defense spending in 2025.
metrics.interpretation: Different definition from SIPRI; never add or average the two.

metrics.label: Global military spending — SIPRI
metrics.definition: SIPRI estimate of global military spending for 2025.
metrics.interpretation: Methodological alternative to IISS, not additional spending.

metrics.label: Developing-country external debt
metrics.definition: World Bank November 5, 2026 reported external debt outstanding in developing countries.
metrics.interpretation: Overlaps with the global debt figure; not interchangeable with external debt service.

metrics.label: Developing-country debt payments
metrics.definition: World Bank principal and interest paid in 2025 by low- and middle-income countries.
metrics.interpretation: Debt service is a yearly payment flow and not the same as outstanding principal.

metrics.label: World economic output (GDP)
metrics.definition: World GDP in nominal current U.S. dollars for calendar year 2025, displayed as trillion-dollar annual production; World Bank estimate.
metrics.interpretation: GDP is value added over a year, not cash available to spend or a stock of wealth. It cannot be added to assets, corporate revenues, or government spending.

metrics.label: U.S. economic output (GDP)
metrics.definition: U.S. GDP in nominal current U.S. dollars for calendar year 2025.
metrics.interpretation: A geographical subset of world GDP and not an additive second global total. Annual economic output is not equivalent to federal budget outlays.

sourceCorrections.sourceRow: Trillions source spreadsheet: US healthcare spending, $5.3T, year 2025
sourceCorrections.resolution: Correct to $5.7T estimated for calendar-year 2025 using June 2026 CMS projection; $5.3T refers to 2024

sourceCorrections.sourceRow: Trillions spreadsheet: all billionaires, $20.1T, data year 2025
sourceCorrections.resolution: The $20.1T / 3,428 people corresponds to Forbes 2026 list using 2026-03-01 wealth snapshots
Subtotals have source/year inconsistencies: use Forbes 2026 source-specific $8.4T / 989 U.S. billionaires for comparable 2026 data

sourceCorrections.sourceRow: Trillions spreadsheet: two incompatible 2026 federal-debt entries ($31T, $38T)
sourceCorrections.resolution: Hold from direct comparison until federal total / debt held by public and measurement date are reconciled with Treasury

sourceCorrections.sourceRow: Trillions spreadsheet: 2026 wealth of Elon Musk listed as $1.2T
sourceCorrections.resolution: Exclude without dated source verification and definition; billionaire net worth fluctuates and is not cash
Pledged divestment of assets by investors is not the same as actually divested dollars; avoid describing as funds moved

sourceCorrections.sourceRow: Trillions spreadsheet: $42T offshore wealth from inflation-adjusted 2012 estimate
sourceCorrections.resolution: Legacy estimated range with transformed price basis; avoid presenting as current measured offshore wealth

sourceCorrections.sourceRow: Trillions spreadsheet: $32.6T Medicare for All 10-year projected spending
sourceCorrections.resolution: Gross program spending scenarios are not net incremental taxpayer costs or household savings; hold pending source-specific treatment

sourceCorrections.sourceRow: Trillions spreadsheet: $208.3T wealth of 1% described as everyone above $1M
sourceCorrections.resolution: 1%-wealth and millionaire threshold are not definitionally identical; withhold until original UBS report and population basis confirmed

sourceCorrections.sourceRow: Trillions spreadsheet: climate spending/savings from 2015–2020 proposals
sourceCorrections.resolution: Historical model scenarios; suitable as dated scenario studies only, not 2026 project costs or completed benefits

sourceCorrections.sourceRow: Trillions spreadsheet: World GDP $112T listed for 2025
sourceCorrections.resolution: World Bank WDI reports $118.35T for 2025; approximately $111.67T corresponds to 2024. Use 2025 value, correct date.

recommendedProductConnections: Economic fragility / household and sovereign debt
publicationRule: Any comparison must state year, geography, stock-vs-flow and uncertainty. Do not imply these figures prove monopolistic harm or political corruption.
